Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the call today — quick recap from our side and an ask so we can scope the POC:

- Primary business goal: reduce manual triage for inbound clinical messages by ~60% while keeping extraction accuracy high for ICD codes and patient identifiers.
- Success criteria we care about:
  - Extraction accuracy (entity-level F1) >= 0.92 on a held-out labeled set
  - End-to-end p50 latency <= 250ms for single-message inference (EU region)
  - Throughput target: support bursts to 20 qps without significant p95 latency degradation
  - No clinical PHI leaves EU region; retention 30 days max in logs

We have an historical dataset of ~12k anonymizable messages; we can provide labels for a 10k sample if that helps.

Next steps we want from Redwood: a recommended evaluation approach (offline batch vs shadow), a one-page success matrix and proposed timeline, and who from your side will own config + infra during the POC.

Can you send over those two options and a recommended plan by EOD Wednesday? Tom (procurement) is looped for any contract/NDAs.

Best,
Emily

Thanks Emily — great summary. Short answer up front: we recommend a two-stage POC (offline batch eval -> short live shadow) for this use case; below is the rationale and a proposed timeline. Attached: POC-success-matrix.xlsx and eval-rubric-v1.pdf.

High-level options (pros/cons):
1) Offline batch evaluation (recommended first step)
   - Pros: fast, deterministic, uses your labeled historic data (privacy-preserving if we run in your VPC), gives a clear accuracy baseline vs acceptance matrix
   - Cons: doesn’t exercise live latency/throughput or upstream integrations

2) Online shadowing (non-blocking live traffic)
   - Pros: measures latency and behavior on real distribution, surfaces infra and caching edge cases
   - Cons: requires safer rollouts (no responses sent to users), slightly more setup time and infra coordination

Recommended plan (hybrid, 3 weeks):
- Week 1: Offline eval — run Redwood predictions on a 10k labeled sample, grade with our rubric, tune model variant/quantization. Owner: Karthik (SE).
- Week 2: Shadow deployment in your EU VPC (non-serving) for 5 business days, observe p50/p95, collect edge-case failures. Owner: Jonas (infra).
- Week 3: Wrap, acceptance checklist, and remediation plan if gates not met. Owner: Lauren (AM).

Minimum deliverables:
- Acceptance matrix (pass/fail per criterion)
- Graded rubric spreadsheet (scored by human review)
- Latency/throughput dashboard snapshot
- Data retention and anonymization report

Open items:
- Can you confirm whether we should run the offline eval inside your VPC (preferred) or if you will provide a secured sample externally?
- Please confirm the 10k labeled subset availability and expected delivery date.

If that plan looks good I’ll send a short charter and an action tracker. Proposed kickoff: Monday 2026-12-07.

Thanks,
Lauren
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Adding some SE-level constraints and checklist so we have a clear acceptance flow for the offline work:

- Data & labels: need CSV (id, message_text, label_json) or newline-delimited JSON; 10k sample is ideal but 5k minimum for statistical confidence.
- Anonymization: please remove direct identifiers or mark them with <PHI> tokens; if you prefer we can run our anonymization script inside your VPC. See attached anonymization-checklist.txt.
- Metrics: we’ll compute entity-level precision/recall/F1, and a small set of downstream metrics (triage reduction simulated throughput).
- Sampling: ensure distribution covers both high-frequency and long-tail message types — otherwise offline accuracy will be biased.
- Latency caveat: offline eval won’t expose first-token generation caches — shadow stage needed to validate p50/p95.

Technical resources we’ll need from MediLink for shadow: short-lived service account for read-only logs, a small k8s namespace for sidecar capture (if allowed), and network peering details for EU region testing.

I’ll prepare a SE runbook and a script to score outputs; anticipate ~2 business days to get baseline offline results once we have the labeled set.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
